newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Counties board urges arbitrage rebate relief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Counties board urges arbitrage rebate relief.

text.p: Leaders of the 3,072 U.S. counties on Sunday voted to urge the U.S. Congress to ease arbitrage rebate restrictions on state and local governments, the officials said.

Arbitrage is the practice of selling tax-exempt bonds and investing the proceeds in higher-yielding taxable securities. Localities are barred by the U.S. Congress from selling tax-exempts just to make arbitrage profits.

The board of directors of the National Association of Counties (NACo), which met this past week at NACo's annual legislative conference here, approved a draft resolution urging Congress and the administration to back an amendment to the U.S. tax code on arbitrage rebate.

The amendment would permit a state, county or city to determine at the time they issue their bonds whether a rebate is owed, the draft resolution says. Currently, rebate is calculated much later in the bond issuance process.

The amendment also urges Congress to develop simpler and clearer procedures for counties and cities to follow when determining whether a bond issue qualifies for an arbitage rebate exception, the draft says.
NACo's board also said it wants Congress to set up a federal fund to help states and localities leverage bond issues to finance school repair, renovation, mondernization and construction projects.
In his fiscal 1998 U.S. budget requestion, President Clinton proposed such a school construction fund. Further details on the plan are expected soon.

NACo's board also urged Congress and the administration to continue to fund two key housing programs administered by the Department of Housing and Urban Development - HOME and community development block grants - at their current levels.
HOME gets $4.6 billion and CDBG gets $1.4 billion, plus annual increases indexed to the Consumer Price Index.
NACo's full membership will take a final vote on the draft policies at the group's annual meeting in July.
A NACo aide said this year's legislative conference, with over 2,600 attendees, is the largest in the group's history.
